pages.title: Magnetic Monopole
pages.text: A magnet with only one pole. Maxwell's equations would be beautifully symmetric if these existed, and Dirac showed a single one anywhere would explain why electric charge comes in fixed units. A compass near it points straight at it, no matter where I stand.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Smashing Quark-Gluon Plasma in the Quark-Gluon Collider, I aimed a superconducting coil at the debris. One particle threaded the coil and left a permanent jump in the current: the signature of a monopole, just as Cabrera once looked for.
